en.desktop.newind.eft.desc: The Fisher Transform is a technical indicator created by J.F. Ehlers. It converts prices into a Gaussian normal distribution. In this way, the indicator highlights when prices have moved to an extreme, based on recent prices. This may help in spotting turning points in the price of an asset. It also shows the trend and isolates the price waves within a trend.
en.desktop.newind.eft.name: Ehler Fisher Transform
en.desktop.newind.ema.desc: The Exponential Moving Average (EMA) gets smoothed as it calculates the current average value by considering its own value for the previous period. In the process of smoothing, the priority decreases exponentially and never equals zero.
en.desktop.newind.ema.name: EMA
en.desktop.newind.hma.desc: Hull Moving Average (HMA) is a fast and smooth moving average that eliminates lags and improves smoothing at the same time. A longer period HMA may be used to identify trends, while a shorter period HMA may be used for entry signals in the direction of the prevailing trend.
en.desktop.newind.hma.name: HMA
en.desktop.newind.hml.desc: High - Low is an indicator that displays the maximum and minimum of the price over a certain period of time. High and low prices can serve as benchmarks in analyzing the market and act as key levels.
en.desktop.newind.hml.name: High - Low
en.desktop.newind.rma.desc: The Rainbow Moving Average indicator displays multiple simple moving averages (SMAs) at once over a specific period of time to make it even easier to identify trends. Each SMA is calculated based on the previous SMA and is color-coded to look like a rainbow.
en.desktop.newind.rma.name: Rainbow Moving Averages
en.desktop.newind.sar.desc: Support and Resistance are significant levels on the asset chart that the price has a chance of retracing from. Trading on breakouts and trend reversals is a popular method of choosing market entries.
en.desktop.newind.sar.name: Support and Resistance
en.desktop.newind.sma.desc: The Simple Moving Average (SMA) formula is the average closing price of a security over the last "x" periods. By averaging prices, it follows the primary trend of the market, always with a certain delay, filtering out smaller fluctuations. The shorter the simple moving average, the faster it determines the new trend, but at the same time it reacts to more false fluctuations, and vice versa, the longer the moving average, the slower it determines the new trend, but you get fewer false fluctuations.
en.desktop.newind.sma.name: SMA
en.desktop.newind.smr.desc: Combining Stochastic, MACD, and RSI indicators provides valuable insights into market conditions, trends, and entry/exit points. By considering overbought/oversold levels, trend confirmation, and momentum, you make informed decisions with improved accuracy and timing.
en.desktop.newind.smr.name: Stochastic+MACD+RSI
en.desktop.newind.srp.desc: Supercharge your analysis with the Simple Reversal Point strategy. Spot trend reversals, boost reliability with confirmation from other indicators, and achieve perfect entry and exit points for optimized trading performance and maximized returns.
en.desktop.newind.srp.name: Simple Reversal Point
en.desktop.newind.tma.desc: The Triangular Moving Average (TMA) is basically a double-smoothed simple moving average that gives more weight to the middle part of the data interval. Since the primary purpose of the TMA is to double smooth the price data, the indicator does not respond well to the latest price fluctuations, so it is not well suited to fast-moving markets. However, the TMA lag can also be an advantage: if the price is moving back and forth, the TMA won't react as much, letting you know that the trend hasn't changed.
en.desktop.newind.tma.name: TMA
en.desktop.newind.tws.desc: The “Three White Soldiers” is an automatic strategy that suggests a possible shift in the trend. It’s created by three consecutive green candles and indicates that buyers might be gaining strength, possibly leading to a price increase.

en.desktop.indinfo.soldiers: Three White Soldiers is a candlestick pattern in trading that consists of three consecutive bullish candles with increasing closing and opening prices above the previous day. This pattern signals a strong bullish sentiment in the market and can indicate a continuation of an uptrend. Traders may use this pattern to identify entry points in the market to potentially profit from the continuation of the upward price movement.

en.desktop.newind.alma.desc: The ALMA indicator was developed in an attempt to create a new moving average that would have superior smoothness and responsiveness as compared to other moving averages. It uses a Gaussian distribution to direct the moving average towards the most current prices. This allows you to use larger timeframes to filter out all “noise”, while the indicator responds promptly to changes in market trends.
en.desktop.newind.alma.name: Arnaud Legoux Moving Average (ALMA)
en.desktop.newind.cccd.desc: The Consecutive Candle Count (CCC) is a technical analysis indicator that focuses on identifying potential trend reversals. It analyzes consecutive candlesticks to determine the prevailing trend and assess the likelihood of a reversal. By observing the pattern of consecutive bullish or bearish candles, traders can gain insights into the strength of the current trend and anticipate potential changes in direction.
en.desktop.newind.cccd.name: CCC
en.desktop.newind.dogi.desc: A Doji candlestick pattern is a Japanese candlestick pattern that occurs when the opening and closing price of an asset are very close or exactly the same, resulting in a candlestick with a very small or non-existent body and long wicks or shadows. The Doji candlestick pattern is significant because it suggests indecision in the market, and it may indicate that a trend reversal could be imminent.
en.desktop.newind.dogi.name: Doji
en.desktop.newind.emac.desc: The EMA crossover strategy uses multiple Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs) with different periods to analyze price trends and generate trading signals. By comparing shorter-term EMAs with longer-term EMAs, you can identify potential entry and exit points based on crossovers and trend confirmations. This strategy filters out market noise and helps you capture trends, providing a clearer market direction.
en.desktop.newind.emac.name: EMA Cross
en.desktop.newind.kama.desc: Kaufman's Adaptive Moving Average (KAMA) is a complex trend indicator that comes as an adaptive moving average. KAMA is not sensitive to insignificant fluctuations in the market, which helps eliminate many false trading signals. The indicator is perfect for determining the dominant trend in the market.
en.desktop.newind.kama.name: Kaufman's Adaptive Moving Average (KAMA)
en.desktop.newind.lsma.desc: The Least Square Moving Average (LSMA) is based on the use of the least square method. The moving average will continue to move in the direction of the trend even after the trend has stopped. This indicator will therefore show what might happen if the trend continues.
en.desktop.newind.lsma.name: Least Squares Moving Average (LSMA)
en.desktop.newind.rahd.desc: The Regular and Hidden Divergence Indicator helps identify potential trend reversals and continuations. Regular divergence signals a potential trend reversal, allowing early entry or exit before major price shifts. Hidden divergence suggests trend continuation, helping you stay in profitable trends longer. Using this indicator enhances market insight, improving decision-making and profit opportunities.
en.desktop.newind.rahd.name: The Regular and Hidden Divergence Indicator
en.desktop.newind.ravi.desc: The RAVI indicator helps identify trends in the market. The indicator shows the difference (in percentage) between the current prices and the past prices. Two key lines are 3% or 1% in dependence on the market. A bull trend begins when the RAVI crosses the 3% key line from bottom-up. The bull trend is considered active if the indicator line moves up. A bear trend begins when the RAVI crosses the 1% key line from top to downside. The bear trend is considered active if the indicator line moves down.
en.desktop.newind.ravi.name: RAVI
en.desktop.newind.ssma.desc: Smoothed Simple Moving Average (SSMA) takes into account a large number of candlesticks on record and is extremely smoothed.
en.desktop.newind.ssma.name: SSMA
en.desktop.newind.tbcp.desc: The “Three Black Crows” is an automatic strategy that indicates a potential trend change. It is formed by three consecutive red candles and means that the price might go down because sellers are getting stronger.
en.desktop.newind.tbcp.name: Three Black Crows
en.desktop.newind.trix.desc: TRIX is a momentum oscillator that displays the percent rate of change of a triple exponentially smoothed moving average. It was developed in the early 1980s by Jack Hutson, an editor for Technical Analysis of Stocks and Commodities magazine. With its triple smoothing, TRIX is designed to filter out insignificant price movements.
en.desktop.newind.trix.name: TRIX
en.desktop.newind.vwma.desc: The Volume Weighted Moving Average (VWMA) is an indicator that can detect emerging trends, identify current trends, as well as the end of a trend. Its principle is similar to that of a simple moving average, and they are usually used together. The difference between them is the effect of volume weighting. For example, if the VWMA moves below the SMA, it might mean that the trend lacks volume support. Their divergence could be used as a signal to go against the trend.
en.desktop.newind.vwma.name: VWMA

The Ichimoku Cloud, or Ichimoku Kinko Hyo, is quite a versatile indicator that combines features of a trend indicator and an oscillator. Ichimoku helps analyze the dynamics of currency pairs, determine the direction of the trend, and detect support and resistance levels.

The Ichimoku Cloud is based on moving averages and is most often used for daily and weekly timeframes.

en.desktop.newind.aroon.desc: Aroon is an indicator that allows you to predict changes in prices, the direction of the trend and its strength. The indicator is used to determine the weakening of the trend and predict its subsequent change or development. It is usually visualized as two lines: AroonUp (red) shows the number of periods since the daily maximum, and AroonDown (blue) shows the number of periods since the daily minimum.
en.desktop.newind.aroon.name: Aroon
en.desktop.newind.bb_pb.desc: Bollinger Bands %B is almost a complete analog of the classic Bollinger Bands, with the only difference that %B is designed for line charts. Both indicators show absolutely identical values ​​— the moments when the price leaves the corridor. The enhanced version of Bollinger Bands eliminates the need to search for exit points when they are hard to see — everything is much clearer when displayed in a separate window and as a line chart.
en.desktop.newind.bb_pb.name: Bollinger Bands %B
en.desktop.newind.dpoma.desc: This strategy combines Moving Average and DPO indicators to help you spot trend changes and potential reversals in the price direction. It offers insights into overall trend direction and highlights trade opportunities with visual shapes and colors. It generates buy (long) and sell (short) signals, guiding your decisions for potential entry and exit points.
en.desktop.newind.dpoma.name: Force of Two
en.desktop.newind.tdseq.desc: The TD Sequential identifies price exhaustion points through number sequences. A Buy Setup forms when nine consecutive bars close lower than four bars earlier, while a Sell Setup forms when nine bars close higher. After a setup, a Countdown phase begins, tracking 13 more bars to confirm trend exhaustion. Once conditions are met, buy or sell signals appear as visual markers on the chart. Traders use it to spot potential reversals and trend continuations.
en.desktop.newind.tdseq.name: TD Sequential
en.desktop.newind.vidya.desc: The Variable Index Dynamic Average (VIDYA) indicator is a relatively new method of calculating the exponential moving average (EMA) with a dynamically changing averaging period. The averaging period depends on market volatility, with Chande Momentum Oscillator (CMO) selected as a measure of volatility. This oscillator measures the ratio between the sum of positive increments and the sum of negative increments over a certain period (CMO period). The CMO value is used as a coefficient to the EMA smoothing factor. Thus, the VIDYA indicator has only two settings: the CMO period and the exponential moving average smoothing period (EMA period)
en.desktop.newind.vidya.name: VIDYA

en.desktop.newind.dimacd.desc: DiNapoli MACD is a modified version of the MACD indicator that helps traders identify trend strength and potential reversals. It utilizes smoothing techniques and unique parameters to improve accuracy. Traders use it to spot buying and selling signals based on moving average convergence and divergence.
en.desktop.newind.dimacd.name: DiNapoli MACD
en.desktop.newind.harami.desc: The Harami is a candlestick pattern in technical analysis that can show a potential trend reversal. It consists of two consecutive candles, where the first candle is larger and encompasses the second candle, which is smaller and located within the body of the first candle. This pattern can be either bullish or bearish, depending on the direction the trend occurs in. It suggests a potential weakening of the previous trend and a possible reversal in the near future.
en.desktop.newind.harami.name: Harami
en.desktop.newind.macdbb.desc: Our strategy combines MACD and Bollinger Bands indicators to enhance investment analysis. It helps identify trends, assess momentum, spot reversals, manage volatility, and pinpoint entry/exit points. By leveraging these indicators together, investors can make more informed decisions and improve their overall trading performance.
en.desktop.newind.macdbb.name: MACD+BB
en.desktop.newind.median.desc: The Simple Moving Median trading indicator is very similar to SMA (Simple Moving Average), but instead of returning the average price it returns the median price. A median is conceptually similar to an average except that an average is affected by outliers while a median is not. It is calculated by sorting all the numbers in the series and picking the number in the middle.
en.desktop.newind.median.name: Median
en.desktop.newind.qstick.desc: Qstick Indicator is a technical analysis tool developed by Tushar Chande to identify trends in candlestick charting. It is calculated by taking an 'n' period moving average of the difference between the open and closing prices. A Qstick value greater than zero means that most of the last 'n' days have been up, indicating that buying pressure has been increasing.
en.desktop.newind.qstick.name: Qstick
en.desktop.newind.sqzmom.desc: The Squeeze Momentum can indicate a period of low volatility and impending breakout in a trading instrument. It occurs when the Bollinger Bands narrow, signifying a reduction in price volatility. It suggests that the market is in a state of consolidation and is likely to experience a significant price movement soon. Traders often use it as a signal to anticipate potential breakouts or trend reversals. It can help identify periods of potential opportunity and guide trading decisions based on the anticipated expansion in price volatility.
en.desktop.newind.zigzag.desc: The ZigZag indicator plots points on the chart whenever prices reverse by a percentage greater than a pre-chosen variable. Straight lines are then drawn, connecting these points. The indicator is used to help identify price trends. It eliminates random price fluctuations and attempts to show trend changes. ZigZag lines only appear when there is a price movement between a swing high and a swing low that is greater than a specified percentage; often 5%. By filtering minor price movements, the indicator makes trends easier to spot in all time frames.
en.desktop.newind.zigzag.name: ZigZag

en.desktop.newind.distoch.desc: The DiNapoli Preferred Stochastic Oscillator is a modified version of the stochastic oscillator. It reduces noise and provides ideas for identifying overbought and oversold conditions. Traders use it to spot potential trend reversals and determine entry and exit points.
en.desktop.newind.std_dev.desc: Standard Deviation is an indicator that measures the scale of price deviation related to the moving average. This means that if the indicator's value is large, the market is experiencing high volatility and candlesticks are well dispersed around. Conversely, if the value is smaller, market volatility is low and prices are relatively close to the moving average. The standard deviation indicator is easy to interpret since it reflects market behavior, which itself consists of shifts between highly active and sluggish market conditions.

en.desktop.newind.stochma.desc: Combining the Stochastic Oscillator with Moving Averages offers a balanced trading approach by integrating momentum and trend direction analysis. The Stochastic Oscillator signals overbought and oversold conditions for potential market reversals, while Moving Averages smooth out price trends to reveal overall trend direction. Together, they help traders better time their entries by understanding both short-term conditions and broader trend movements.

en.desktop.cb_faq_description_1:
Cashback is a reward program where traders can earn back {PERCENT}% of the money they deposited to the platform. To get the reward, you need to reach the turnover of {WAGER} times the deposit over {TTL} days.

For example, in case of a $10 deposit, the turnover must be ${WAGER}0. Note that it's not necessarily a ${WAGER}0 profit — losing trades also count.
en.desktop.cb_faq_description_2: Just make a deposit. The system automatically enables the Cashback feature for your account.
en.desktop.cb_faq_description_3: We credit cashback only for trades on options.
en.desktop.cb_faq_description_4: One cashback period lasts {TTL} days starting from the moment you hit the Cashback button. After that, the icon will turn into a progress bar where you can see how much time is left and how much turnover must be generated.
en.desktop.cb_faq_description_5:
Turnover is the sum of all your investments on all your trades, regardless of its outcome. It means that even if you lose a trade, the invested amount will be reflected in the turnover and count for the Cashback program.

Note that only net-out trades will be taken into account within one expiration. I.e., two trades opened in different directions on the same asset within the same expiration will not be counted in turnover.

Examples:

1. You open just one $100 PUT trade within one expiration. The turnover will be $100.
2. Within one expiration you open trades in opposite directions, for example a $100 PUT and a $50 CALL trade, in this case your turnover will be zero.
en.desktop.cb_faq_description_6: Yes, you can withdraw your cashback anytime. This also applies to the initial deposit used as the base for calculating your cashback turnover. As soon as you have reached the ×{WAGER} turnover goal, the cashback will be credited to your trading balance. From there, you can withdraw it immediately.
en.desktop.cb_faq_description_7: Yes. The number of cashback rounds is unlimited — once your {TTL}-day cashback period is over, you're free to start again.
en.desktop.cb_faq_description_8: If you have met the cashback requirements, the money in the amount of {PERCENT}% of your initial deposit will be credited to your account immediately.

en.desktop.newind.bb_width.desc: Bollinger Bands Width (BBW) is a technical analysis indicator derived from the standard Bollinger Bands. Bollinger Bands are a volatility indicator that forms a band of three lines plotted in relation to the price of a security. The middle line is usually a 20-day simple moving average. The upper and lower bands are usually 2 standard deviations above and below the SMA (middle line). The Bollinger Band Width is used to measure the width between the upper and lower bands and can be used to determine trading signals.
en.desktop.newind.bb_width.name: Bollinger Bands Width
en.desktop.newind.demarker.desc: The DeMarker is an overbought/oversold indicator created with the purpose of identifying potential minima and maxima of the market based on demand. en.desktop.newind.atr_bands.desc: ATR Bands is an indicator that is designed to be used along with the average true range (ATR) indicator. The ATR bands are plotted around the ATR values to indicate the direction of movements in price.
en.desktop.newind.atr_bands.name: ATR Bands
en.desktop.newind.chop_zone.desc: Chop Zone is a visual indicator designed to identify trends and choppiness. When plotted within -100/+100 levels, the Chop Zone displays the difference between the closing price and its EMA by presenting its values as colors.
en.desktop.newind.chop_zone.name: Chop Zone
en.desktop.newind.engulfing.desc: Engulfing pattern is a candlestick pattern indicating a possible trend reversal. It happens when a larger candle fully engulfs a smaller candle in the opposite direction. A bullish engulfing suggests a potential shift from a downtrend to an uptrend, while a bearish engulfing indicates a potential reversal from an uptrend to a downtrend. Traders use the Engulfing pattern to identify significant market reversals and make trading decisions based on the potential trend change.
en.desktop.newind.engulfing.name: Engulfing
en.desktop.newind.envelopes.desc: Envelopes are technical indicators that are typically plotted over a price chart with upper and lower bounds. The most common example of an envelope is a moving average envelope, which is created using two moving averages that define upper and lower price range levels. Envelopes are commonly used to help traders and investors identify extreme overbought and oversold conditions, as well as trading ranges. Traders can interpret envelopes in many ways, but most use them to define trading ranges.
en.desktop.newind.envelopes.name: Envelopes
en.desktop.newind.gridlines.desc: The “Grid Line V2” indicator plots horizontal lines on price charts to mark potential support and resistance levels, helping traders spot possible price reversals or slowdowns. Red lines below the central gray line (based on the 4-hour opening price) act as support levels, while green lines above indicate resistance levels. Though it uses a 4-hour timeframe, it can be applied to various timeframes and combined with other indicators for enhanced market analysis.
en.desktop.newind.gridlines.name: Grid Lines
en.desktop.newind.linreg_r2.desc: This indicator consists of a median line with 2 parallel lines above and below it at the same distance. These lines can be considered as support and resistance. The median line is calculated based on a linear regression of the closing prices, but the source can also be set to open, high or low. The height of the channel is based on the deviation of the price from the median line. Extrapolating the channel forward can help to provide bias and find trading opportunities.
en.desktop.newind.linreg_r2.name: Linear Regression R2
en.desktop.newind.mamacdeng.desc: The strategy combines Moving Average, MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence), and Engulfing Candlestick pattern indicators to capitalize on market trends and reversals.
en.desktop.newind.mamacdeng.name: MA+MACD+Engulfing
en.desktop.newind.momentums.desc: Momentum Strength is a measure used in technical analysis to assess the strength and speed of price movements in a financial market. It helps traders determine the level of enthusiasm or conviction behind a price trend. High Momentum Strength indicates a strong and potentially sustainable trend, while low Momentum Strength suggests a weaker or less reliable trend.
en.desktop.newind.momentums.name: Momentum Strength
en.desktop.newind.special_k.desc: Special K is a momentum indicator that combines short-, intermediate- and long-term velocity into one complete series. It has two functions: first, to identify primary trend reversals at a relatively early stage; second, to use that information for timing short-term pro-trend price moves.
en.desktop.newind.special_k.name: Special K
en.desktop.newind.timeframe.desc: The Timeframe Indicator displays a line that changes color based on whether the closing price increased or decreased, allowing quick visual identification of market direction. It supports multi-timeframe analysis by letting you view and select different time frames on one chart to suit various strategies. This customizable indicator aids in understanding trends for better risk management and can be combined with other tools without cluttering your workspace.
en.desktop.newind.timeframe.name: Timeframe

en.desktop.newind.darvas_box.desc: The Darvas Box indicator uses a series of five states to draw the upper and lower lines of a box by finding highs and lows. The Darvas Box indicator is drawn with a green upper band and a red lower band overlaying a candlestick chart. Buy signals are drawn in green arrows beneath the candles, while sell signals are drawn with red arrows above the candles.
en.desktop.newind.darvas_box.name: Darvas Box
en.desktop.newind.lowest_low.desc: Lowest Low means that stock has hit an all-time low since it is listed, and it indicates the decrease in demand at that time of the given stock. The Lowest Low-Value indicator simply returns the lowest low price over a user-defined n-period.

en.desktop.newind.mass_index.desc: Mass Index is an unconventional oscillator that is designed to detect market trend reversals by changing the width of the range between the maximum and minimum prices. The mass index increases with the expansion of the range and decreases with its narrowing. The most valuable signal Mass Index gives is the so-called “reversal hunch” where the index first grows to 27 and then falls below 26.5.
en.desktop.newind.mass_index.name: Mass Index
en.desktop.newind.net_volume.desc: Net Volume is a security's uptick volume (the volume of shares traded while a stock price is rising) minus its downtick volume (the volume of shares traded while a stock price is falling) over a specified period of time. The net volume of a stock aggregates the total positive and negative movements of the asset over this period. When the total upward movement is greater than the total downward movement over this period, the stock has a positive net volume.
en.desktop.newind.net_volume.name: Net Volume
en.desktop.newind.supertrend.desc: The Supertrend is a trend-following indicator that behaves similarly to moving averages and MACD. It is plotted on prices, and their placement indicates the current trend. This indicator is easy to use and gives an accurate reading about an ongoing trend. It is constructed with two parameters: period and multiplier. The default values used are 10 for average true range or trading period and three for its multiplier.

en.desktop.newind.bullandbear.desc: Bull Bear Power is a trading indicator that measures the strength of bullish and bearish forces in the market. It helps traders identify potential trend reversals and confirm the strength of existing trends. By incorporating Bull Bear Power into their strategy, traders can make more informed decisions about entry and exit points, trend confirmation, and risk management.
en.desktop.newind.bullandbear.name: Bull and Bear Power
en.desktop.newind.starc_bands.desc: STARC Bands are basically three lines that form a channel around a simple moving average. STARC bands are narrowing in stable markets and expanding in volatile markets. When the price crosses the boundaries of the STARC bands, you'll get a signal recommending opening a buy or sell transaction. The other purpose this indicator can serve is to help identify overbought or oversold zones.
en.desktop.newind.starc_bands.name: STARC Bands
en.desktop.newind.swing_index.desc: The Swing Index is a technical indicator that attempts to predict future short-term price action: when the Swing Index crosses above zero, a trader can expect short-term price movement to move upward. When the Swing Index crosses below zero, a trader might expect short-term price movement to be downward.
en.desktop.newind.swing_index.name: Swing Index
en.desktop.newind.tii.major_period: This index is designed to help determine the strength of a trend. The major period dictates the period over which the moving average is calculated. A major period of 60 is recommended.
en.desktop.newind.tii.minor_period: This index is designed to help determine the strength of a trend. The minor period dictates the period over which the sum of the deviations of price from the given moving average will be calculated. Minor period of 30 is recommended.
en.desktop.newind.ulcer_index.desc: The Ulcer Index (UI) is a technical indicator that measures downside risk in terms of both the depth and duration of price declines. The index rises as the price moves away from a recent high and falls as the price rises to new highs. The indicator is usually calculated over a 14-day period, with the Ulcer Index showing the percentage drawdown a trader can expect from the high over that period. The higher the value of the Ulcer Index, the longer it will take for a stock to return to its previous high.
en.desktop.newind.ulcer_index.name: Ulcer Index
en.desktop.newind.woodies_cci.desc: Woodies CCI is a momentum indicator, a modified version of Commodity Channel Index. The indicator consists of two CCI lines with periods 6 and 14. The fast curve is used to predict the direction the slow one will take. The values of Woodies CCI fluctuate around the zero line and do not have high and low limits. A high value indicates that the price of the security is overbought at the moment, a low value is a signal of overbought price. The key levels of Woodies CCI are + -100, + -200 and the zero line.
en.desktop.newind.woodies_cci.name: Woodies CCI

en.desktop.newind.linreg_slope.desc: Linear regression is a statistical tool used to help predict future values from past values. It is commonly used as a quantitative way to determine the underlying trend and when prices are overextended. A linear regression trend line uses the least squares method to plot a straight line through prices to minimize the distances between the prices and the resulting trend line.  This linear regression indicator plots the slope of the trend line value for each given data point.
en.desktop.newind.linreg_slope.name: Linear Regression Slope
en.desktop.newind.pivot_points.desc: Pivot points refer to technical analysis indicators or calculations used to determine the overall market trend over various time intervals. The pivot point itself is simply the average of the previous trading day's high, low, and close prices. Trading above the pivot point the following day is considered to indicate continued bullish sentiment, while trading below the pivot point is considered to indicate bearish sentiment.
en.desktop.newind.pivot_points.name: Pivot Points
en.desktop.newind.supandresist.desc: Support and resistance are key levels in trading where the price tends to stop, reverse, or consolidate. Traders use them to make better trading decisions and manage risk. Support acts as a floor, preventing prices from falling further, while resistance acts as a ceiling, preventing prices from rising further. Identifying these levels helps traders determine entry and exit points in their trades.

en.billing.deposit.bonus.faq.answer1:
A bonus is an additional amount of funds that you receive on the real account and can use for trading on the platform.

There are two types of bonuses on the platform:
- Deposit bonuses — you need to make a deposit to get them.
- No deposit bonuses — you do not need to make a deposit.

After you receive a bonus, the trading rules are the same for both types (wager, turnover, and cancellation rules).
en.billing.deposit.bonus.faq.answer2: Click the Add Bonus button while making a deposit. You can make several deposits with the bonus, but the bonus will be applied only to the first deposit that is successfully processed. If you do not want to participate in the bonus program, you can always make a deposit without a bonus.
en.billing.deposit.bonus.faq.answer3: The amount of the bonus depends on the deposit you make. Note that the bonus amount cannot exceed %max_amount.
en.billing.deposit.bonus.faq.answer5: You can use the bonus funds to trade on the platform.
en.billing.deposit.bonus.faq.answer6: Withdrawals are only available once you have reached the indicated turnover or canceled the bonus.
en.billing.deposit.bonus.faq.answer7: The required trading turnover equals the bonus amount multiplied by the wager, where the wager value = %wager. Note that only option trades on the real balance, closed by expiration, are taken into account. The following trades are excluded from the turnover calculation: margin trades, trades closed by buyback, trades in opposite directions within the same asset and expiration, trades closed with the “equal” result.
en.billing.deposit.bonus.faq.answer8: Click the Cancel bonus button located under the bonus icon in the upper-right corner of the traderoom. If you have open trades, you need to close them to cancel the bonus.
en.billing.deposit.bonus.faq.answer9: If your balance is zero, the bonus will only be canceled if you have no open positions. In this case, you will be excluded from the current bonus program. You can receive a new bonus if you make another deposit.

This indicator allows users to select a timeframe and plots a line on the chart based on closing values. The line changes color depending on whether the closing value increased or decreased.

Benefits for traders:

Multi-Timeframe Analysis: View different time frames on one chart to identify trends and short-term signals simultaneously.
Adaptability: Choose from various time frames to suit different market conditions and trading strategies.
Visual Indicators: Quickly identify market direction with color-coded lines, aiding in swift decision-making.
Efficiency: Streamline workflow by integrating information directly into the chart, saving time.
Customization: Extend or combine with other indicators for complex strategies.
Risk Management: Understand long-term trends alongside short-term movements for better risk management.
Confirmation: Identify stronger setups by spotting signals on multiple time frames.
Overlay: Doesn't clutter the workspace with additional sub-charts, allowing for cleaner analysis.

Using RSI and MACD together enhances trading decisions:
Confirmation: Aligned signals boost confidence in trading decisions.
Divergence: Identifies powerful reversal signals.
Trend Confirmation: MACD confirms trend direction; RSI indicates overbought or oversold levels.
Timing Entries and Exits: RSI for timing; MACD for trend reversals or continuations.
Risk Management: Helps set stop-loss and take-profit levels.
Versatility: Applicable across different markets and timeframes.
en.desktop.indicators.rsi-or-macd.name: RSI OR MACD
en.desktop.indicators.scripts_tdi.desc: TDI (Traders Dynamic Index) is a unique indicator that blends RSI, Moving Averages, and Bollinger Bands into one clear chart. Originally developed for forex trading, TDI helps identify trend direction, strength, and potential reversals in real time, making it especially useful in volatile markets.
en.desktop.indicators.scripts_tdi.name: Scripts TDI
en.desktop.indicators.ssl_channel.desc: With its unique algorithm, the SSL Channel Indicator plots a dynamic channel on your price chart, representing the market's trend and volatility. It provides clear signals for potential breakouts, reversals, and trend continuation, giving you an edge in your trading decisions.
en.desktop.indicators.ssl_channel.name: SSL channel
en.desktop.indicators.vwap_signal.desc: Two VWAP lines show you the average price weighted by volume—fast for quick moves, slow for the bigger trend. Buy signals appear when price crosses above the fast VWAP and fast is above slow. Sell signals trigger when price drops below fast VWAP and fast falls under slow. Clear entry and exit points based on volume-confirmed price action.
en.desktop.indicators.vwap_signal.name: VWAP Signal System

en.desktop.newind.acc_swing_index.desc: The Accumulative Swing Index is used to assess the long-term trend by comparing the bars that were at the opening and closing highs and lows. If the ASI is positive, we can assume that the long term trend is up and if the ASI is negative, we can assume that the long term trend is down. This indicator is mainly used as a divergence and confirmation tool, but can also be used as a signal to buy or sell.
en.desktop.newind.acc_swing_index.name: Accumulative Swing Index
en.desktop.newind.disparity_index.desc: The Disparity Index is a technical indicator that measures the relative position of an asset's last closing price to a selected moving average and expresses the value as a percentage. A value greater than zero - a positive percentage - shows that the price is rising, indicating that the asset is gaining upward momentum. Conversely, a value less than zero - a negative percentage - can be interpreted as an indication that selling pressure is increasing, causing the price to fall. A value of zero means that the current price of the asset is exactly in line with its moving average. Extreme values in either direction may indicate that a price correction is imminent.
en.desktop.newind.disparity_index.name: Disparity Index
en.desktop.newind.elder_ray_index.desc: The Elder Ray Index is designed to measure the amount of buying and selling power in a market. It has both a bullish and bearish component, which are plotted as two separate indicators. One is termed “bull power,” while the other is called “bear power.“ The bull power indicator functions by showing the relation between the daily high and an n-period exponential moving average. The bear power indicator functions by showing the relation between the daily low and an n-period exponential moving average. Bull Power = Daily High–EMA (of n-periods); Bear Power = Daily Low–EMA (of n-periods).
en.desktop.newind.elder_ray_index.name: Elder Ray Index
en.desktop.newind.know_sure_thing.desc: The KST is a two-line indicator like the MACD. The oscillator swings above and below zero and accordingly gives trade signals to traders. If the Know Sure Thing crosses above the zero line, then a buy signal is triggered. If the KST holds above the zero line for an extended period, an uptrend is confirmed. Conversely, if the KST crosses below the zero line, then a sell signal is triggered. Moreover, if the KST remains below the zero line, the downtrend is confirmed.
en.desktop.newind.know_sure_thing.name: Know Sure Thing
en.desktop.newind.linreg_forecast.desc: Linear regression is a statistical tool used to help predict future values from past values. It is frequently used as a quantitative way to determine the underlying trend and when prices are overextended. A linear regression trend line uses the least squares method to plot a straight line through prices to minimize the distances between the prices and the resulting trend line.
en.desktop.newind.linreg_forecast.name: Linear Regression Forecast

en.desktop.indicators.golden_cross.desc: This EMA strategy uses multiple moving averages to spot trend direction and trading signals. Crossovers between short- and long-term EMAs help identify entry and exit points while filtering out market noise.

en.desktop.indicators.winning_line.desc: Like a finely tuned engine paired with perfect grip, momentum and trend move as one. MACD shows momentum shifts, Moving Averages set the pace, and together they give you the traction to handle any market curve.

en.desktop.newind.aroon_oscillator.desc: The Aroon Oscillator is based on the Aroon Indicator and is useful for identifying whether the market is on a downtrend, uptrend, or sideways phase. This allows traders to know when it is appropriate to use trend-following tactics and when not beforehand. If the Aroon Oscillator line is above zero, this may be interpreted as a bullish signal. If it is below zero, it is most likely an indication of a bearish trend. The farther the oscillator line is from the zero level, the stronger the trend is. If the indicator value is near the zero line, there is no trend in the market.
en.desktop.newind.aroon_oscillator.name: Aroon Oscillator
en.desktop.newind.balance_of_power.desc: The Balance of Power (BOP) is an oscillator that shows whether bears and bulls of the Forex market can reach new extreme price levels. Traders may use this indicator to help identify the direction of a trend, find divergences between the price and the BoP in order to identify a potential trend reversal or trend continuation setup, and take advantage of overbought and oversold conditions.
en.desktop.newind.balance_of_power.name: Balance of Power
en.desktop.newind.choppiness_index.desc: The Choppiness Index (CHOP) is an indicator designed to determine whether the market is choppy (trading sideways) or not choppy (trading within a trend). CHOP is not meant to predict future market direction but is rather used for defining the market's trendiness. A basic understanding of the indicator would be; higher values equal more choppiness, while lower values indicate directional trending.
en.desktop.newind.choppiness_index.name: Choppiness Index
en.desktop.newind.gator_oscillator.desc: The Gator Oscillator helps detect trend changes in the asset price using a histogram. The Gator Oscillator is based on the principle that trends—just like a living alligator—go through four different phases: Sleeping (exhausted), Awakening (forming), Eating (Strengthening) and Sated (running out of momentum).
en.desktop.newind.gator_oscillator.name: Gator Oscillator
en.desktop.newind.keltner_channels.desc: The Keltner Channel is a classic technical analysis indicator that consists of three lines: the middle line is a 10-day simple moving average for “typical” ((high + low + close) / 3) prices, the upper and lower lines are calculated by adding and subtracting the moving average daily price range (the difference between the maximum and minimum) from the middle line. Thus, you get a channel based on volatility. The classic strategy for this indicator is to buy when closing above the top line and sell when closing below the bottom line.
en.desktop.newind.keltner_channels.name: Keltner Channels
en.desktop.newind.linreg_intercept.desc: The Linear Regression Intercept indicator plots the intercept for the trend line for each data point. It is commonly used as a quantitative way to determine the underlying trend and when prices are overextended. A linear regression trend line uses the least squares method to plot a straight line through prices to minimize the distances between the prices and the resulting trend line.
en.desktop.newind.linreg_intercept.name: Linear Regression Intercept
en.desktop.newind.mcginley_dynamic.desc: The McGinley Dynamic indicator looks like a moving average, but in fact it is a price smoothing mechanism that tracks changes much better than any moving average. This indicator minimizes price differences automatically, which allows you to avoid false signals.
en.desktop.newind.mcginley_dynamic.name: McGinley Dynamic
en.desktop.newind.price_oscillator.desc: The Price Oscillator is an indicator that uses two moving averages: one is shorter-period and the other is longer-period. It calculates the difference between the two moving averages and can indicate areas of overbought and oversold conditions while attempting to confirm bullish or bearish price moves.
en.desktop.newind.price_oscillator.name: Price Oscillator
en.desktop.newind.vortex_indicator.desc: A vortex indicator (VI) is composed of two lines—an uptrend line (VI+) and a downtrend line (VI-). These lines are often colored green and red, respectively. A vortex indicator is used to spot trend reversals and confirm current trends.
en.desktop.newind.vortex_indicator.name: Vortex Indicator
en.desktop.newind.weis_wave_volume.desc: Weis Wave Volume is an indicator that takes market volume and organizes it into wave charts, clearly highlighting inflection points and supply/demand areas. It works with all time periods and can be applied to the futures, forex, stock, and commodity markets. The main purpose of the indicator is to identify turning points.
en.desktop.newind.weis_wave_volume.name: Weis Wave Volume

en.desktop.platform.indicators.hint-adx: Average Directional Movement Index (ADX) is always ahead of the curve and shows the strength of trend (upward/downward trend or weakening) prior to the start of the price movement. ADX indicator can also be used to identify potential changes in market volatility.
en.desktop.platform.indicators.hint-atr: Unlike most indicators, the Average True Range (ATR) cannot predict the movement direction. It displays exclusively the current volatility of the trading asset within the selected period. Moreover, ATR determines the quote change rate. Active movement of ATR indicates an increase in the range of candlesticks.
en.desktop.platform.indicators.hint-cci: The CCI belongs to the class of oscillators that measure the speed of price movement. The CCI is designed to identify impending market reversals. It can be used to assess the strength of the current trend or to identify extremes (minimum and maximum prices). In general, the CCI is very similar to the ADX and can also be used as a tool to determine the market trend, as its rate of change depends on the strength of the current market trend.
en.desktop.platform.indicators.hint-rsi: The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is used to determine the strength of the current trend and its possible reversal points. RSI compares the absolute asset price growth within a certain time period with the total price reduction within the same period. The result is visualized as a curve on the chart with a range of 0 to 100%.

en.desktop.indicators.rsi+cci+bb+ma.desc: These indicators (RSI, CCI, BB, and MA) help traders analyze market trends and make better trading decisions by identifying overbought/oversold conditions, spotting potential reversals, gauging volatility, and determining price trends.

en.desktop.indicators.stochastic+ma.desc: The Stochastic Oscillator provides signals for overbought and oversold conditions, indicating potential market reversals. On the other hand, Moving Averages smooth out price trends, offering insights into the direction of the trend. Combining these two indicators is advantageous because it provides a comprehensive understanding of both momentum and trend direction in the market. Stochastic identifies short-term market conditions, while Moving Averages offer a broader perspective on trend movements. Together, they offer a balanced approach to trading decision-making, allowing traders to better time entries

en.desktop.newind.center_of_gravity.desc: The Center of Gravity (CoG) is a channel indicator that determines the limits of price fluctuations and measures the level of volatility of the traded asset. Based on moving averages, it calculates the “center” of the price and builds price channels that serve as corridors for asset quotes.
en.desktop.newind.center_of_gravity.name: Center of Gravity
en.desktop.newind.chande_kroll_stop.desc: The Chande Kroll Stop is a trend-following indicator that identifies the stop loss for a long or short position by using a variation on directional movement. It is calculated on the average true range of an instrument's volatility. The indicator comes with a long stop line (blue) and a short stop line (red), placing the stops under (and on) the high (low) of the last “n” bars.
en.desktop.newind.chande_kroll_stop.name: Chande Kroll Stop
en.desktop.newind.donchian_channels.desc: The Donchian Channel is a volatility indicator that forms a price range on the chart at a given time, based on the highs and lows of the previous period. The indicator is displayed as two lines—the upper and the lower—based on the highest and lowest price values of the previous trading period. The best possible period to use with the Donchian Channel is 20.
en.desktop.newind.donchian_channels.name: Donchian Channels
en.desktop.newind.random_walk_index.desc: The Random Walk Index (RWI) is a technical indicator that attempts to determine if a stock's price movement is random or nature or a result of a statistically significant trend. The Random Walk Index attempts to determine when the market is in a strong uptrend or downtrend by measuring price ranges over N and how it differs from what would be expected by a random walk (randomly going up or down). The greater range suggests a stronger trend.
en.desktop.newind.random_walk_index.name: Random Walk Index
en.desktop.newind.volume_oscillator.desc: The Volume Oscillator is an indicator that shows the difference between the two trading volumes. The basic idea of the oscillator is to track the dominant trend in trading volume changes. When the fast-moving average is higher than the slow one, the oscillator keeps above zero, showing a tendency to increase in volume. If the oscillator is below zero, it means that the moving averages changed places and the volume falls.
en.desktop.newind.volume_oscillator.name: Volume Oscillator

en.desktop.newind.chaikin_volatility.desc: Chaikin Volatility indicator takes into account changes in the spread between the maximum and minimum prices to determine the intensity of volatility. At the same time, it avoids price gaps, which makes it different from Average True Range (ATR).
en.desktop.newind.chaikin_volatility.name: Chaikin Volatility
en.desktop.newind.klinger_oscillator.desc: The Klinger Oscillator shows the difference between the two distant trading volumes of an asset. The indicator is designed for short- and medium-term analysis; it is sufficiently sensitive to short-term peaks and bottoms and accurately identifies the long-term trend of money flow.
en.desktop.newind.klinger_oscillator.name: Klinger Oscillator
en.desktop.newind.prime_number_bands.desc: The Prime Number Bands indicator shows the space range where a market price moves into. This indicator uses prime numbers and identifies the closest high and low prime numbers. It also plots the difference between the values at the given moment.
en.desktop.newind.prime_number_bands.name: Prime Number Bands
en.desktop.newind.psychological_line.desc: Psychological Line Indicator is the ratio of the number of rising periods over the total number of periods. It reflects the buying power in relation to the selling power. If PSY is above 50%, it indicates that buyers are in control. Likewise, if it is below 50%, it indicates the sellers are in control. If the PSY moves along the 50% area, it indicates a balance between the buyers and sellers and therefore there is no direction movement for the market.
en.desktop.newind.psychological_line.name: Psychological Line
en.desktop.newind.rainbow_oscillator.desc: The Rainbow Oscillator calculates and displays the highest high and lowest low of one or more simple moving averages to determine market trends. The oscillator curves are created based on the moving average calculations. The high and low oscillator curves are color-coded on the chart and market trends can be determined based on the width of the curves.
en.desktop.newind.rainbow_oscillator.name: Rainbow Oscillator
en.desktop.newind.schaff_trend_cycle.desc: The Schaff Trend Cycle (STC) indicator is an oscillator commonly used to identify market trends and provides buy and sell signals to traders. The STC assumes that currency trends accelerate and decelerate in cyclical patterns that may reflect the dominant price cycle of any currency during any timeframe. The STC detects upwards and downwards trends long before the moving average convergence/divergence (MACD), an indicator that is notorious for lagging due to its slow responsive signal line.

en.desktop.newind.chande_forecast_osc.desc: The Chande Forecast Oscillator is calculated as a percentage difference between the expected price and the current price of the security. The oscillator is above zero when the forecasted value is above the current price. When the forecasted value is above the current price, the indicator is below zero. When the current price of an instrument for a certain period of time is below the oscillator's forecast, this means that we could expect price declines in the future. In the opposite situation, we could predict a rise in prices.
en.desktop.newind.chande_forecast_osc.name: Chande Forecast Oscillator
en.desktop.newind.chande_momentum_osc.desc: The Chande Momentum Oscillator, or CMO, is a technical momentum indicator by Tushar Chande. The CMO is created by calculating the difference between the sum of all recent higher close prices and the sum of all recent lower close prices and then dividing the result by the total sum of price movement over a time period. The result is multiplied by 100 to give the -100 to +100 range. The defined time period usually equals 20 periods.
en.desktop.newind.chande_momentum_osc.name: Chande Momentum Oscillator
en.desktop.newind.fractal_chaos_bands.desc: The Fractal Chaos Bands indicator connects the highest/lowest price points on an interval with two lines and creates a band. The upper fractal line is created by plotting the high prices and the lower fractal line is created by plotting the low prices. The flatter the band, the more volatile the movement. The more the band resembles a staircase, the more trendy the movement. The bands provide an overview of the price movement by filtering out the insignificant price fluctuations.
en.desktop.newind.fractal_chaos_bands.name: Fractal Chaos Bands
en.desktop.newind.relative_volatility.desc: The Relative Volatility Index (RVI) is a volatility indicator that was developed by Donald Dorsey to indicate the direction of volatility. The RVI is plotted in a range from 0 to 100 and is often used as a confirmation for other indicators and is often used in conjunction with moving average (MA) crossover signals. It is calculated in the same way as the RSI but using the standard deviation of high and low prices rather than the absolute change in price. This indicator is designed not as a stand-alone indicator but as a confirmation for other indicators.
en.desktop.newind.relative_volatility.name: Relative Volatility
en.desktop.newind.ultimate_oscillator.desc: The Ultimate Oscillator is a technical indicator developed by Larry Williams in 1976 to measure the price momentum of an asset across multiple timeframes. By using the weighted average of three different timeframes, this indicator has less volatility and fewer trade signals compared to other oscillators that rely on a single timeframe. Buy and sell signals are generated following divergences. The indicator uses three timeframes in its calculation: 7, 14, and 28 periods.
en.desktop.newind.ultimate_oscillator.name: Ultimate Oscillator

en.desktop.newind.divergence_indicator.desc: The Divergence indicator denotes a class of indicators, the aim of which is to depict the earlier signs of how forex will change in the future. At the moment of its turn, as a rule, the market reaches a peak and lets them know that there is no more power needed to keep on increasing. The most popular price divergence example is when the market shows a higher maximum but an indicator does not depict it, on the other hand, calculating a lower maximum. It means that very soon the price may become lower. It is called a bearish divergence signal. The other example is when there are lower minimums on the market, though a chart shows a higher minimum. The phenomenon is known as bullish divergence.

en.desktop.newind.elder_impulse_system.desc: The Elder Impulse System is based on two indicators: a 13-day exponential moving average and a MACD histogram. en.desktop.newind.relative_vigor_index.desc: The Relative Vigor Index (RVI) is a technical analysis indicator that measures the strength of a trend by comparing a security's closing price to its trading range and smoothing the results. It's based on the tendency for prices to close higher than they open in uptrends and to close lower than they open in downtrends. The RVI indicator is calculated similarly to the stochastic oscillator, but it compares the close relative to the open rather than comparing the close relative to the low.

en.desktop.newind.historical_volatility.des: The Historical Volatility (HV) is a statistical measure of the dispersion of returns for a given security or market index over a given period. It is calculated by determining the average deviation from the average price of a financial instrument in the given time period. The standard deviation is a way to calculate historical volatility. The higher the historical volatility value, the riskier the security is. However, that is not necessarily a bad result, as risk works both ways—bullish and bearish.
en.desktop.newind.trend_intensity_index.des: The Trend Intensity Index (TII) is used to indicate the strength of the current trend in the market. The stronger the current trend, the more likely it is that the market will continue to move in the current direction. It is recommended to enter the market during a strong trend and ride it until the TII shows signs of a reversal, at which point one should exit the current position and prepare to enter in the opposite direction.

en.desktop.margin_balance.margin_level_tool: The Margin Level indicates the impact of your currently open CFD positions on your account. en.desktop.newind.intraday_momentum_index.d: The Intraday Momentum Index, or IMI, is a technical indicator that combines aspects of candlestick analysis with the relative strength index (RSI). This indicator is used for providing investors with a way to find optimal days to buy and sell. The Intraday Momentum Index looks at the relationship between a stock's open and close price over the course of the day and combines some features of the relative strength index, namely the relationship between up closes and down closes and whether there is an indication that a stock is overbought or oversold, with candlestick charts.
en.desktop.newind.prime_number_oscillator.d: Shows the difference between the nearest prime number and the price series. en.desktop.newind.true_strength_indicator.d: The True Strength Index (TSI) is a technical indicator used in the analysis of financial markets that attempts to show both trend direction and overbought/oversold conditions. The TSI combines various factors to create an indication of price and direction more in sync with market turns than any moving average.

en.desktop.newind.gopalakrishnan_range_inde: The Gopalakrishnan Range Index, or GAPO, attempts to determine the variability of price data based on the log of the price range over a user-defined n-periods. The Gopalakrishnan Range Index is intended to measure volatility in a stock or commodity. The indicator is calculated over a set time period (default 5 periods) using only price action. Gopalakrishnan Range Index calculates the natural logarithm of the highest high minus the lowest low and divides the result by the natural logarithm of the number of periods.
en.desktop.newind.vertical_horizontal_filte: The Vertical Horizontal Filter (“VHF”) determines whether prices are in a trending phase or a congestion phase. While trend-following indicators such as the MACD and moving averages are excellent in trending markets but generate multiple conflicting trades during trading-range (or “congestion”) periods, and RSI-alike oscillators usually close positions prematurely during trending markets, the VHF attempts to determine the “trendiness” of prices and thus determine which indicator to use in the given situation.
